discovery: Cosmic inflation and the quantum origin of cosmic structure
motivation: Guth proposed that an early epoch of exponential expansion driven by a scalar field resolves the horizon, flatness and monopole problems, changing how we think about the initial conditions of the universe. Linde made the idea workable with new and chaotic inflation, which established the slow-roll paradigm that underlies all current models. Mukhanov (with Chibisov) showed that quantum vacuum fluctuations stretched during inflation seed the density perturbations, and he predicted a nearly scale-invariant spectrum with a small red tilt. COBE, WMAP and Planck confirmed these predictions: the perturbations are adiabatic, nearly Gaussian and super-horizon, with n_s ≈ 0.965, measured to be below unity at high significance. Inflation links quantum field theory at the highest energies to the largest observable structures. It is a rare case of a bold theoretical proposal whose quantitative consequences were verified by precision measurements, and it now frames how particle physics and cosmology ask their central questions.
